Month → Week → Day is the only flow that keeps my brain calm. 🗓️ Monthly planner: appointments, quizzes, group meetings, anything not fully in my control 📆 Weekly planner: flexible blocks so I can prep before deadlines hit 📝 Daily pages: only 3 timed anchors + micro-step to-dos for dopamine If you have ADHD, executive dysfunction, or you keep making to-do lists you can’t finish—try this. ADHD weekly planning routine that actually works 🧠✨ My everyday planner-> @Sugar Paper LA  If your weeks feel chaotic, this simple system helps you reset, refocus, and stay on track without overwhelm. Here is the weekly planning flow: 1. Brain dump everything on your mind 2. Pick a theme for each day of the week so your week has structure 3. Add your tasks into Google Tasks under each day or theme 4. Break everything into small doable steps 5. Time block your most important work so it actually gets done This is not about being perfect. It is about giving your ADHD brain a simple structure that makes the week feel easier to manage. Save this for your weekly reset and follow for more simple productivity systems for ADHD brains 💛 #ADHDPlanning #WeeklyPlanning #ProductivitySystem #ADHDTools #ExecutiveFunction

I think I accidentally created my new favorite way to use a Hobonichi Weeks. 👀📓 I’m calling it Analog Weeks, a planner dedicated to slowing down, living more offline, and actually documenting the little parts of life I usually forget. Each day gets its own loose theme: Reset Monday. Tiny Joy Tuesday. Without Wi-Fi Wednesday. Thoughtful Thursday. Five Senses Friday. Side Quest Saturday. Soft Sunday. And instead of filling the blank page with another giant to do list, I’m using it for things like offline hours, little things I noticed, what I’m currently using, weekly keepsakes, and one ordinary moment I want to remember. Because maybe our planners don’t always have to help us do more. Maybe sometimes they can help us notice more. Would you start an Analog Weeks with me? #HobonichiWeeks #AnalogLife #JournalingIdeas #StationeryTok #SlowLiving
